title: Post-incident synthetic test generation for config-triggered quality regressions
creator: Asha Mehta
description: After a recent production incident where a configuration change correlated with a sharp drop in answer-precision for a subset of customer prompts, we need a formalized post-incident flow that generates targeted synthetic tests and differential evals to (1) rapidly triage config vs model-induced regressions, (2) create repeatable tests for CI, and (3) produce a prioritized remediation/rollback signal for the rollout pipeline.
background: On 2026-02-17 an autoscaling/serving config tweak (shorter KV cache TTL + adaptive batching thresholds) coincided with a 12% degradation on our alerting eval for the "financial_faq" dataset. Root cause analysis was inconclusive: signals pointed to both changed runtime behavior (cache misses) and a new model variant rollout earlier that week. Existing eval harness lacks the ability to synthesize request variants that exercise the TTL and batch shape distribution, and we had no quick way to run differential snapshots across config permutations.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible script that generates synthetic prompt permutations from a failed eval snapshot and can parameterize config variables (KV TTL, batching thresholds, prefix caching enabled/disabled).

An automated differential-eval job that runs the synthetic tests against two runtime configs (pre-change and post-change) within the CI environment and produces a small human-readable regression report.
Tests added to the evals suite for the top 3 failure modes from the incident (cache-related token drop, length-dependent hallucination, truncated context behavior).
Runbook entry added with repro steps and a dashboard link; playbook includes rollback criteria and quick mitigation toggles.
A PR with the implementation and an accompanying perf/cost sanity check merged into main.
tasks: Triage incident artifacts and extract representative failing requests from the alert window (owner: Liam).
Design a lightweight synthetic prompt generator that can mutate length, tokenization boundary positions, and prefix context (owner: Asha).
Implement parameterized harness that spins up two config variants in the staging runtime and runs diff-eval (owner: Eng-Test infra).
Hook the diff-eval into the CI with a PR-build guard and an opt-in nightly job for regression collection (owner: CI infra).
Document runbook and escalate criteria; link dashboards and previous incident notes (owner: SRE).
comments: 2026-02-20: Initial triage complete — pulled 210 unique failing requests from the 10:00-11:30 PST window. Pattern: longer prompts (>512 tokens) show increased hallucination after the config change.
2026-02-21: Decision: build synthetic generator around token-boundary mutations instead of full paraphrase generation — quicker to iterate and isolates cache/KV behaviors.
2026-02-22: Prototype synthetic generator ready; generated 3 families of variants (length + prefix shift + repeated tokens). Local repro shows 9% delta when toggling KV TTL from 60s -> 5s.
2026-02-24: Infra note: staging runtime will require a lightweight isolation profile to run two configs side-by-side; ENG-20858 has partial work for config isolation, marking as dependency.
2026-02-26: PR opened for diff-eval harness (runtime-eval/PR#45). Running full suite overnight to capture stability. Next: formalize thresholds for automated rollback signal.
2026-02-27: SRE suggested adding an emergency toggle to disable adaptive batching during rollout as a short-term mitigation; adding to runbook TODOs.
